title: Advantage creation
lead: Which actions and players knock the defense out of balance (defender beaten, help drawn, switch), and what that is worth.

blocks.text: An advantage is a moment when the defense is out of balance: the man with the ball has beaten his defender, or a second defender has had to come, or a screen has forced a switch. This tab marks, for every pick, handoff, drive, isolation, post-up and off-ball screen, whether one of those happened in the next 2 s, and asks who creates them and with what.

Thresholds: beaten = more than 1 ft nearer the hoop than his own defender; help drawn = two defenders within 6 ft at once; each must last about 0.3 s. A post-up or a pick naturally has two defenders near the ball (the screener's man), so 'help drawn' means different things for different actions; compare players within an action type.

blocks.text: The aggregates have no 'advantage' flag, but two columns describe beating a defender: SkillCorner's blow-by rate on drives (league 21%) and the ball handler's points per direct pick (league 0.70). Rates are shrunk toward the league with 40 events of prior weight so small samples do not top the list.

sections.title: What this shows and does not

blocks.text: It shows which actions and players knock the defense out of balance by a simple, checkable rule. It does not account for who is guarding the creator, the shot clock, or whether the advantage was used.

If this becomes the topic: define the advantage against the defense's expected position (where it usually stands given the ball and the attackers), and credit the player whose action caused it; then follow the advantage through passes to the shot.
